hypothesis: A versioned replayable commit envelope plus durable request-outcome reconstruction can make Cell v0 lost-reply, resolver, log-tag, generation, and quorum invariants executable before a production WAL exists.
learned: Recovery must rebuild both retained client outcomes and the previous committed log-chain head; the envelope must carry replayable conflict and mutation payloads rather than only their digest.

hypothesis: A logical row oracle can freeze exact base-plus-tail semantics, snapshot retention, and certified-write validation before a DataFusion physical operator exists.
learned: Invalidation must precede predicate and projection; analytical-tail GC is independent from recovery-WAL pop; an active lease fixes object closure; dependency validation and write must be one serializable transaction.

hypothesis: A versioned checksummed local frame plus per-file synchronization and matching-quorum reconstruction can persist the frozen commit envelope, rebuild retained retry outcomes after fresh opens, and reject unsafe suffixes before a consensus library is selected.
learned: Quorum durability should be reconstructed from matching bytes rather than trusted from a self-declared disk certificate; incomplete final frames may be ignored, while complete corruption without a remaining quorum and envelope-chain disagreement must halt recovery. Consensus, network replication, elections, and independent failure domains remain unproven.

hypothesis: An objectKV-owned append-only per-node journal can satisfy OpenRaft 0.9.25 storage-v2 semantics and recover durable vote, committed position, append, conflicting-suffix truncate, purge, and corruption state across fresh opens before networked consensus exists.
learned: The consensus library expects obsolete appends below the durable purge marker to be harmless and same-or-lower retained suffix appends to durably replace that suffix. The objectKV journal can encode both safely while rejecting gaps above the retained log. This admits per-node stable storage only; quorum commit, elections, network faults, generation takeover, and real process crash remain unproven.

hypothesis: Three OpenRaft nodes using objectKV per-node journals and a seeded Turmoil TCP network can preserve quorum-acknowledged commits through leader isolation, successor election, partition repair, stale-suffix replacement, simulated process crash, bounce, and restarted-node catchup.
learned: A single explicit election trigger can arrive before the prior committed-vote lease permits takeover; the deterministic controller must keep the event explicit while retriggering until the recorded successor state is observed. The cluster safely replaces an isolated uncommitted suffix after a higher-term quorum commits. This admits simulated runtime crash and real-journal reopen only; real OS process kill, unsynced-disk loss, generation takeover, and durable request-outcome integration remain unproven.

hypothesis: A versioned request identity and replay-built outcome inside the replicated OpenRaft application history can survive a lost reply, real leader-process kill, successor retry, and killed-node restart without applying the logical command twice.
learned: A durable retry outcome can be rebuilt by replaying the committed log into a fresh state machine, but the eval must wait through the duplicate log index before judging recovered state or it can sample midway through replay. This admits normal TCP and real OS process death; state-machine snapshot persistence, outcome expiry, automatic election, generation takeover, independent-disk loss, and object-store recovery remain unproven.

hypothesis: A replicated external authority plus a data-log fence barrier can move one cell from Active through Fencing and Recovering, reject a preauthorized G1 write ordered after the barrier, survive authority-leader loss, hand the voter set from G1 to G2, and resume with one exact log.
learned: An external linearizable authority read alone has a cross-consensus TOCTOU window. The old transaction system must also commit a replicated data-log fence barrier, and its state machine must reject stale client entries ordered after that barrier before recovery is reserved. This admits a quiesced real-process voter-set takeover. Automatic failure detection, authenticated fence and recovery certificates, control-root reconciliation, coordinator membership change, independent-disk loss, and object-store recovery remain unproven.

hypothesis: Distinct data voters can sign exact locally applied fence and voter-set positions so the external generation authority can reject controller-fabricated recovery evidence before reserving or activating a transaction-system generation.
learned: A signer must attest the exact applied barrier or voter-set transition, not merely a lower position it has applied past. The certificate must bind purpose, cell, generation, recovery identity, active and pending transaction-system identities, membership, and Raft position. Real-process election terms can vary across replays, so the semantic trace normalizes terms while certificate verification still binds the exact observed term. Production key custody, control-root reconciliation, and independent-disk recovery remain unproven.

hypothesis: A custom DataFusion TableProvider and ExecutionPlan can preserve the frozen exact-snapshot contract across a schema-v1 Parquet base and schema-v2 Arrow tail before streaming or pruning optimizations exist.
learned: DataFusion still pushes output projection into a scan when filters remain unsupported, so the provider must add projection above the hidden-column overlay. Its Parquet reader defaults strings to Utf8View, which the v1-to-v2 normalizer must either accept or explicitly disable. DataFusion 54.0 also admits incompatible 54.1 internal crates unless the complete family is lockfile-pinned. The exact physical contract is possible, but this correctness adapter materializes bounded inputs and admits no performance curve yet.

hypothesis: A transactional publication intent, named immutable-object verification, complete reachability walk, quarantine interval, and delete-time root-domain revalidation can prevent premature visibility and live-object deletion despite unknown PUT outcomes, GC races, counter drift, stale LIST responses, interrupted marks, and root changes.
learned: An uploaded block needs a transactional in-flight root before GC can race it. Accounting counters and LIST observations cannot determine liveness, a partial mark reclaims nothing, and every delete plan must be revalidated after a root-epoch change. This deterministic model admits the contract only; a real object client, durable transactional authority, independent process failure, and guarded delete worker remain unproven.

hypothesis: A DataFusion execution plan can merge schema-normalized Parquet base rows and Arrow table changes incrementally across arbitrary record-batch boundaries, preserve one target version across independent partition watermarks and continuation, and declare ordered output without materializing either complete input.
learned: With skewed physical-partition bases, the first exact global identity stream must read the tail from min(W_p), even though that replays changes already reflected in newer bases. Logical-id reduction must cross Arrow batch boundaries, continuation must retain T, and output ordering is safe to declare only after validating both input orders across batches. This admits bounded operator buffering and exactness only; manifest and lease acquisition, multiple execution ranges, partition-aware pruning, full-query memory, and a T-minus-W performance curve remain unproven.

hypothesis: A real Apache object_store client plus a separately reopened quorum-fsynced local authority can preserve intent-before-upload, exact closure-before-root, unknown PUT and authority outcomes, complete reachability, and safe unguarded deletion when a durable per-digest reservation serializes publication against sweep.
learned: Delete-time root revalidation alone is insufficient for backends without native conditional delete. Publication can start after revalidation, verify the old digest object, and race the unguarded delete. A durable per-digest deletion reservation closes that window by rejecting intersecting publication until delete outcome recovery and retirement. The receipt is same-machine and single-process; replicated transaction authority, independent-disk recovery, process kills, provider-native guarded delete, and cloud cost curves remain unproven.

hypothesis: Publication intents, roots, pins, deletion reservations, and durable request outcomes can share the existing three-node OpenRaft generation authority and survive lost replies, real leader-process death, exact retry, generation transition, and restarted-node replay without exposing a stale or conflicting publication decision.
learned: Publication outcome resolution must be linearizable, reader-visible roots and pins need compare-and-swap, and both intents and deletion permits must remain generation-bound in the same replicated state machine. This admits the authority contract only. Publisher and sweeper process death at object-operation boundaries, authority snapshot and outcome expiry, independent-disk loss, provider-native guarded delete, reservation partitioning, and cloud cost curves remain unproven.

hypothesis: A dedicated publisher process can recover from SIGKILL after quorum-durable Prepare and before the first object PUT, restart with empty scratch, replay the exact canonical job and request identities, verify immutable bytes by named reads, and complete one atomic root publication through the replicated cell authority.
learned: Durable publication state is sufficient to restart a publisher without a worker-local journal at the first effect boundary. The immutable job and transition identities must be derived from canonical bytes, and the controller must prove both the replicated Prepare outcome and object absence before killing the first worker. Partial uploads, lost object or Publish replies, abandoned intents, sweeper receipts, object-effect fencing, authority snapshot repair, and cloud semantics remain unproven.

hypothesis: A publisher can recover from SIGKILL after an immutable data-object PUT takes effect but its response becomes retryable-unknown, restart with empty scratch, recover the canonical job from quorum-durable intent, verify the existing named object exactly, complete the closure, and publish one atomic root.
learned: An unknown object-write response must remain uncertain until exact named identity resolves it. Replicated intent plus deterministic immutable names is sufficient to restart without a worker-local journal, but root publication must remain after a full closure walk. Lost manifest and Publish replies, repeated unknown responses, multipart residue, abandoned-intent reassignment, sweeper recovery, generation-bound effect grants, independent-disk loss, and cloud semantics remain unproven.

hypothesis: A publisher can recover from SIGKILL after the immutable manifest PUT takes effect but its response becomes retryable-unknown, restart with empty scratch, recover the canonical job from quorum-durable intent, verify every data object and the manifest by exact named identity, walk the complete closure, and publish one atomic root.
learned: Manifest identity authenticates only manifest bytes. It does not prove child presence. A replacement can recover safely from replicated intent and deterministic immutable names, but it must replay data identities and walk the complete named closure before requesting visibility. Lost Publish replies, repeated unknown responses, multipart residue, abandoned-intent reassignment, sweeper recovery, generation-bound effect grants, independent-disk loss, and cloud semantics remain unproven.

hypothesis: A publisher can recover after its replicated Publish command applies but its response is lost, then the publisher and accepting authority leader die, by reconstructing the stable job and request identity from empty scratch, resolving the quorum-durable outcome on a successor, and retrying without a second authority or object effect.
learned: A matching current root and complete object closure do not identify the outcome of the original Publish invocation. Safe crash recovery requires a replicated command receipt keyed by a stable identity, exact fingerprint validation, and retry that returns the original applied position without a second state transition. Retained-outcome expiry and snapshot restoration, repeated lost replies, later-root supersession, generation handoff, multipart residue, independent-disk loss, and cloud semantics remain unproven.

hypothesis: Pinned SlateDB can establish a correctness-gated local physical incumbent for deterministic ingest, point reads, ordered scans, and fresh-instance reopen while recording backend requests and bytes through the shared eval and OTel contracts.
learned: A fresh-instance reopen was roughly three orders of magnitude slower than a warm-instance read, so cache state must remain a hard gate. The local incumbent is directionally useful but not a product verdict: raw backend calls include expected absence and conditional-operation failures, compaction is not forced, and remote S3, GCS, scale, and named cost ceilings remain unmeasured.

hypothesis: Pinned SlateDB can reopen from a fresh in-process cache without reading work proportional to all durable bytes as a deterministic dataset grows from 1 MiB to 64 MiB.
learned: The original Phase 0 timing blended close writes with recovery and is superseded. With corrected boundaries, 1 MiB and 8 MiB reopen are metadata-bounded, but the 64 MiB open reads 210,773,938 bytes before the first point lookup. This crosses RFC-0022's stop threshold for the untuned SlateDB incumbent. It does not falsify objectKV; it requires one bounded SlateDB layout and compaction pass before replacing that incumbent.

hypothesis: A complete Cell v0 transaction-authority snapshot can durably bind one applied OpenRaft position, survive removal of all covered journal entries on every voter, restore exact semantic and retry state, and continue committing without weakening the no-snapshot control.
learned: The transaction authority can survive complete covered-log removal in the bounded local process topology when one checksummed, versioned, fsynced snapshot includes applied position, membership, semantic rows, OCC history, commit envelopes, generation and publication state, fingerprints, and retained outcomes. The first JSON-map attempt shut OpenRaft down safely because structured request and byte-vector row keys were not encodable; ordered entry arrays with duplicate rejection fixed the latent boundary. Object-data closure, O_cell, snapshot transfer, independent disks, retry expiry, and snapshot size and latency curves remain unproven.

hypothesis: One exact replicated Cell v0 commit chain can become a verified immutable object closure, advance O_cell independently of the transaction-authority checkpoint, and reconstruct an exact empty-cache worker without permitting unsafe log pop.
learned: The bounded cross-role composition works: committed envelopes from the transaction quorum can be objectified, verified, rooted through a separate generation-fenced publication quorum, and replayed by a fresh worker. Root visibility without closure must not advance O_cell. Object closure through 10 still permits log pop only through the authority snapshot at 8 because retry outcomes and OCC state remain authority-owned. Multi-range closure, snapshot installation, retained-suffix recovery, concurrent publication, and independent failure domains remain unproven.

hypothesis: A blank fresh-identity learner can recover complete Cell v0 transaction authority after covered-log reclamation by installing the durable authority snapshot and replaying the retained Raft suffix, then preserve exact state and outcomes across its own process restart.
learned: Raft membership identity and storage incarnation cannot be conflated. A fresh learner safely receives the authority snapshot at 8, replays retained transaction entries through 10 plus membership entry 11, preserves OCC state, envelopes, and exact outcomes, and restarts from its repaired storage. Full-log replay can reconstruct the same rows but is not evidence for post-reclamation repair and is rejected by the gate. Generation-authorized voter replacement, recovered-position certification, snapshot transfer curves, object-root reconciliation, and independent-disk failure remain unproven.

hypothesis: A healthy Cell v0 quorum can replace one failed voter through a fresh node identity, authority-bound learner admission, exact snapshot-plus-suffix readiness, one idempotent membership transition, and removed-voter fencing without changing the transaction-system generation.
learned: Routine repair and full generation recovery need distinct authority state. The model preserves generation 7 while membership epoch advances exactly 4 to 5, continues commits during learner catchup, and makes finalization idempotent. Same-ID replacement, unauthorized admission, early promotion, stale epoch, competing controller, double finalize, removed-voter commit, and repair without a data quorum all fail bounded controls. This admits the protocol model only; replicated authority commands, cryptographic readiness certificates, real OpenRaft voter promotion, process failure, and repair cost curves remain unproven.

hypothesis: A seven-process same-generation voter replacement can be admitted through the shared eval and telemetry contract.
failure: metric recovery.membership_epoch emitted non-allowlisted backend attribute
learned: The process protocol passed direct traces, but the configured run was ineligible until its membership gauge used the frozen registry's cell and transaction_system attributes.

hypothesis: Routine replacement is semantically exact and fresh-process replayable when raw certificate positions are compared directly.
learned: All semantic checks passed, but an OpenRaft election term varied across fresh processes while the membership indexes and normalized semantic trace remained exact. Raw terms are scheduling metadata, so direct report equality was too strict.

hypothesis: Routine replacement preserves exact semantic history when fresh-process comparison normalizes only election terms and retains all positions, checks, counters, voters, and trace digests.
learned: A healthy data quorum can replace voter 201 with fresh voter 204 through snapshot plus suffix, purpose-bound learner and membership certificates, one idempotent epoch transition, removed-voter fencing, post-repair failover, and replacement restart without changing generation 1. The gate still uses one machine and local files; independent failure domains, remote object transfer cost, signer key management, and authority lease behavior remain unproven.

hypothesis: An objectKV serving worker can keep fresh-instance open metadata-bounded and a cold 1 KiB point read below eight requests and 512 KiB by separating maintenance, using 64 KiB SST blocks and whole-SST Bloom filters, and relying on the replicated objectKV transaction log instead of a duplicate SlateDB object WAL.
learned: The dataset-sized open was a configuration and role-placement failure, not a necessary consequence of object-native serving. The frozen profile reduced fresh-open reads to 402 bytes, first-point bytes by 84.9 percent, total reads by 89.3 percent, writes by 51.3 percent, and first-correct-read latency by 99.1 percent across three seeds. Total requests rose 31.9 percent, so remote request pricing and scan shape remain open. SlateDB stays only as a candidate segment implementation until separate compaction, MinIO, GCS, overwrite, and crash-recovery gates pass.

hypothesis: A coordinator with no embedded worker and a separately built format-compatible worker can compact objectkv-serving-v1 SSTs without breaking exact data or restoring dataset-sized fresh reads.
learned: Local format-compatible role separation is plausible. Eight L0 SSTs compact to one sorted run at 1.027x maintenance write amplification while exact fresh reads remain metadata-bounded. Writable-handle open updates 538 bytes of control metadata, but point and scan reads write nothing. SlateDB remains only a local segment candidate until overwrite pressure, compactor process death and reclaim, MinIO, and GCS gates pass.

hypothesis: A coordinator can reclaim an overwrite compaction from a killed standalone worker process, permit a fresh worker identity to complete the same job, and preserve exact latest values without restoring the fresh-read cliff.
learned: One local standalone worker can die after persisting a Running claim without losing or duplicating the overwrite result. The coordinator reclaims the silent job to Scheduled and a fresh identity commits exact output within 576 to 618 ms. The serving reopen remains metadata-bounded. Coordinator death, abandoned-output GC, concurrent writers, MinIO, GCS, and durable child-process telemetry remain open.

hypothesis: A staged Cell v0 transaction can survive proxy death before and after complete tagged-log durability, remain invisible until every required log set is quorum durable, publish and acknowledge once, and recover exact state in a fresh worker.
learned: Ordering and conflict resolution can be separated from visible commit in the replicated authority. The same transaction identity, version, and envelope survive both proxy crash boundaries; both required tagged-log quorums must exist before rows, visible frontier, and client acknowledgement advance. The bounded receipt binds actual process identities and the exact envelope but is not authenticated against a malicious client. Signed receipts, staged-head abort, generation takeover, multi-record lag and backpressure, repair, partitioned routing, independent hosts, and throughput remain open.

hypothesis: A transaction authority can require independently installed log-set policy and verify process-generated Ed25519 quorum certificates over the exact synchronized staged record before visibility, rejecting forged, duplicated, cross-set, tampered, and obsolete evidence.
learned: Authenticated tLog participation can be separated from proxy trust. The authority validates an exact policy-bound statement, distinct signer identities, Ed25519 signatures, and quorum before publication. Policy commands consume Raft positions but not logical database commit versions, so commit sequence is separated from the envelope's actual authority log index. Production key custody, policy rotation, process-incarnation binding, and generation takeover or safe abort of an incomplete staged head remain open.

hypothesis: An active successor generation can publish the exact fully certified old-generation staged head once after data-log fencing and voter-set handoff, recover a lost takeover reply, reject old-generation publication, and commit the next successor transaction without creating a second history.
learned: A fully certified old-generation staged head can cross a transaction-system generation fence without reconstruction or duplicate publication. The active successor publishes the original immutable envelope and retains the takeover outcome for exact retry. A missing certificate still blocks safely; the next proof must fence the old tLog generation strongly enough to rule out a late quorum before deterministic abort, then extend takeover to a multi-record prefix.

hypothesis: An active successor can safely abort one incompletely certified old-generation staged head after every required tLog set durably fences the generation and one incomplete set proves quorum absence for the exact record.
learned: Quorum intersection turns durable absence into an abort proof only after every old-generation tLog set is durably fenced. The aborted sequence remains consumed, the visible frontier does not advance, and the next transaction chains from the last committed envelope. Production fence authorization, signer custody, arbitrary staged prefixes, lag, repair, and partitioning remain open.

hypothesis: An active successor can recover exactly the longest quorum-present prefix of one bounded staged window, abort the first quorum-absent record and its dependent suffix, retain every outcome, and commit the successor after the consumed window.
learned: A bounded pipelined staged window has one deterministic safe disposition: publish the longest prefix present at quorum in every required set, abort the first record absent at quorum in any set and its dependent suffix, consume every sequence, and block on unknown inventory. Sustained lag, ratekeeping, failed-log repair, moving log sets, production fence authorization, signer custody, independent hosts, and partitioned resolvers remain open.

hypothesis: A replicated pre-allocation ratekeeper can bound retained bytes in every required tLog set during objectification lag, then resume from an authority-authenticated durable pop without losing the exact serving suffix.
learned: Fresh signed quorum capacity can bound exact retained bytes before sequence allocation, and a publication-authority process quorum can authorize deletion without controller trust. Each tLog verifies the pinned authority signer set, exact root reference, manifest bytes, and embedded snapshot frontier before pop. The bounded path remains centralized and same-host; failed-log repair, moving log sets, production key custody, partitioned proxies, independent failure domains, and cloud retention curves remain open.

hypothesis: A failed tLog can be rebuilt as a distinct non-voting learner from one active-quorum-certified retained snapshot, survive restart, and become quorum-certified ready without contributing to capacity, durability, pop, or serving.

discarded_candidates.reason: operation.duration omitted the required result attribute, so no schema-valid result was scored

learned: A learner may retain a stale base while excluded, but readiness must bind the current active frontier. Failure is a policy observation, not proof of death, so distinct identity, storage incarnation, key possession, and a later replicated policy transition carry safety. Commit versions and tLog positions remain separate domains. This gate does not admit live-tail catch-up, chunked transfer, promotion, independent hosts, or production key custody.

hypothesis: A repair-ready tagged-log learner can enter one active log set only after a replicated prepare, a successor-policy stage quorum, and an authority activation quorum, while the removed root remains fenced after restart.
learned: Policy movement must be part of the replicated transaction-authority version order, while tagged-log positions remain independent. Repair readiness, successor staging, and committed activation are separate proofs. The removed root stays fenced after restart, but the bounded path still pauses writes and does not admit live-tail catch-up, chunked transfer, independent hosts, production key custody, or concurrent policy movement.

hypothesis: One failed tLog learner can resume a durable chunked base transfer across restart, catch only the ordered records appended while repair is active, and reach current quorum-certified readiness without contributing to active capacity, durability, pop, or serving quorums.
learned: A failed member can be rebuilt without pausing the active policy for the full copy: durably resume one certified base, transfer only the consecutive live tail, and require a second current-root certificate before readiness. Exact duplicate chunks are idempotent; conflicting duplicates, missing chunks, gapped tails, stale readiness, premature quorum counting, and full base recopy fail closed. Remote transfer, multiple simultaneous repairs, unbounded append, lease expiry, orphan cleanup, independent hosts, production key custody, and simultaneous policy movement remain open.

hypothesis: One hot resolver range can split inside an active transaction-system generation by installing an exact clipped conflict-history snapshot in two empty children, shadowing later work through one predecessor barrier, and activating one immutable map mutation only after every proxy and required tLog set processes it.
learned: Conflict metadata can move online without moving durable database bytes when one map stays authoritative until exact snapshot partitioning, shadow catch-up, ordered proxy propagation, and tLog durability all agree. The bounded result does not establish throughput benefit, controller recovery, merge, concurrent movements, serving-range movement, independent hosts, or production key custody.

hypothesis: Commit-proxy loss can recover safely by fencing the complete transaction-system generation, publishing only the authenticated maximal prefix present at quorum in every required tLog set, abandoning incomplete ticket suffixes, and resolving a fully durable lost reply exactly once through stable request identity.
learned: The conservative FoundationDB-style answer is safe in the bounded objectKV composition: a failed proxy ends the transaction-system generation, incomplete ticket suffixes disappear, fully durable work survives an unknown reply, and successor versions exceed every old issued version. Within-generation exact-batch takeover is an availability optimization, not a correctness prerequisite. Recovery downtime, independent hosts, simultaneous controller failure, production authorization, and signer custody remain open.

hypothesis: Full transaction-system generation recovery remains a viable correctness fallback when recovery work is linear in authenticated retained-tail records, pending tickets, and successor roles, and independent of permanent database size.
learned: Recovery work remains linear and reads zero permanent database bytes in the bounded local path. Retained tLog inventory is the first measured bottleneck: 65,536 records per tLog produce a 3.158-second total median, of which 2.870 seconds is inventory. Pending tickets are flat; topology cost splits between inventory and sequential recruitment. Retain full generation recovery as the correctness fallback, then test compact summaries, checkpoint cadence, parallel recruitment, and independent hosts before adding within-generation exact-batch takeover.

hypothesis: One SlateDB database with many logical range prefixes keeps KV Runtime database, decoded-cache, background-task, and object-family cardinality constant through 1,000 assignments, while database-per-range multiplies those physical costs.
learned: Use one SlateDB database with logical range prefixes as the next KV Runtime default. At 1,000 assignments it held one database, one decoded cache, nine live tasks, and nine object files. Database-per-range multiplied tasks to 8,001 and object files to 9,000, used 7.3 to 10.0 times more RSS per range, and reopened about 35 to 37 times slower. The local debug fixture does not establish production throughput, remote-object economics, mixed-load tail bounds, prefix-aware compaction, or range movement.

hypothesis: ObjectKV-owned MVCC physical keys can preserve exact-version point and ordered range semantics while keeping recent point reads sublinear in retained history depth; unbounded history cost must remain visible in storage and scan receipts.
learned: Keep the objectKV-owned MVCC key encoding for the next prototype. Near-latest cold point p99 rose from 1.85 ms at depth 1 to 6.69 ms at depth 256 rather than scanning every retained version. Storage and scan cost remained linear: depth 256 used 283.47 physical bytes per live byte and one cold 1,024-row scan read 74.0 MB through 1,128 range GETs. The next gate must bind durable snapshot leases to a monotonic minimum-readable version and collect older history during object compaction.

hypothesis: A frozen objectKV retention floor can compact a depth-256 MVCC history toward the configured retained window while preserving exact floor and latest reads, point tombstones, snapshot bounds, publication order, and close plus empty-cache reopen.

operational_limit.finding: Staging sixteen overlapping L0 SSTs with compaction disabled reaches SlateDB serving-profile backpressure before the measurement compactor starts. The accepted fixture stages eight SSTs. Production must compact continuously or rate-limit before this bound.

learned: Keep the frozen-floor MVCC filter for the next prototype. Depth-256 history converged to 1.11x to 1.22x retained logical bytes, and cold scan bytes scaled with the retained window rather than total history. Floor and latest point and range reads, tombstone anchors, expired and future refusal, publication, and reopen stayed exact. This is local filesystem object-store evidence only. Durable replicated lease authority, crash ordering, root-aware object deletion, concurrent writes, range tombstones, MinIO, and GCS remain open.

hypothesis: One replicated publication authority can atomically own snapshot admission, exact object closures, a monotonic read floor, frozen collection jobs, replacement publication, and root-aware object deletion across lost replies, leader replacement, and process restart.

subjects.finding: The lease commit survives failover, but the dropped response has no durable outcome.

learned: Keep the co-located lease and publication authority for the next prototype. Across three seeds, acquire, renew, and collection publication each lost an acknowledged reply and recovered the exact retained outcome after leader replacement. A prepared job stayed at F_job 200 while the live floor advanced to 224; publication moved the top-level root and G to 200 exactly once; lease release invalidated a stale delete mark; and the exact permit survived restart. The remaining gate is the rest of RFC-0060's unsafe process subjects plus composition with the real SlateDB collection worker and remote object storage.

hypothesis: The replicated snapshot and publication authority must fail closed when a lease is backdated, a lease root omits its epoch change, a collection range or input root becomes stale, the physical frontier advances before publication, or a committed retry outcome is lost.
learned: Keep the co-located authority and exact collection token compares. The positive history remained exact after five new bounded fault modes. Every unsafe subject was visible on every seed, including the critical rule that G cannot advance before replacement publication and that a receipt cannot publish after either its range epoch or input root changes. Real SlateDB collector composition, incomplete snapshot restore, worker-local expiry, stale generation, stale delete marks, remote object storage, and required-profile OTel remain open.

hypothesis: A real SlateDB MVCC collector can compact only after receiving an exact replicated collection token, return the exact physical manifest closure, survive publication-authority leader replacement, and advance the authoritative root and collected frontier together.
learned: Keep the staged token-to-physical-closure composition. The worker obtains authorization only after discovering the exact input closure, and the successor authority publishes the exact replacement root with G. Treat the engine-specific closure binder as trusted because the generic authority cannot infer a live SST omitted from a submitted receipt. SlateDB internal latest advances before the objectKV authority root and SlateEngine currently opens internal latest, so authority-rooted serving or isolated staging plus promotion is the next hard gate.

hypothesis: A read-only object base can remain pinned to the exact authority-selected SlateDB manifest after the embedded engine advances internal latest, while verifying the manifest identity and preserving exact retained MVCC reads.
learned: Keep the read-only authority-bound base adapter. It verifies the exact manifest path, length, and SHA-256, rejects cross-database and malformed manifest keys, hides manifests newer than the selected root, and disables WAL replay. M0 remains readable after M1 exists, and both roots preserve exact floor and latest MVCC points and scans. The next hard gate is the Range Engine handoff: M0 plus authenticated txLog tail before publication, M1 plus only the post-M1 tail after publication.

hypothesis: A disposable Range Engine can resolve an authority-published SlateDB base, verify its complete physical closure, authenticate the sparse commit-chain suffix from every required signed txLog quorum, and preserve exact state while the authority replaces M0 with M1.
learned: Keep the authority base plus certified txLog tail handoff. A worker can verify the exact M0 or M1 physical closure and reach the same target through a sparse signed commit chain while one authority leader and one member of each txLog set are unavailable. The result admits semantics only. Collector isolation, old-root reclamation, concurrent application, worker restart, remote request economics, and performance curves remain open.

hypothesis: A dedicated physical collector process can discover an exact SlateDB input closure, obtain its frozen collection token over the replicated authority network before compaction, persist its output after process exit, and let the successor authority publish the independently re-verified closure.
learned: Keep the dedicated collector process. Authorization now crosses the same authority network as other clients, and the controller can independently re-hash both physical closures after the collector exits. Process isolation does not solve reachability or reclamation. Old-root reader pinning, root-walk deletion, concurrent jobs, remote object economics, and required-profile telemetry remain open.

hypothesis: An authority-pinned M0 closure can remain exact across M1 publication, reject every delete while leased, become reclaimable only after release advances the root epoch, and be physically deleted through exact permits without breaking a fresh M1 worker.
learned: Keep the lease-pinned old-root reclamation protocol. A fresh post-GC worker remains exact after every unique M0 object is removed, while bypassed pins, stale mark epochs, and early permit retirement fail independently. The lease represents the reader lifetime, but this history does not keep the original reader process alive during deletion. Concurrent traffic, worker restart, remote request economics, and performance curves remain open.

hypothesis: An authority-bound SlateDB base can open without scanning logical rows, and a real quorum-certified txLog overlay can grow linearly while preserving exact point and ordered range reads.
learned: Keep the base plus certified-tail architecture for the next prototype. Base-only open remained 0.60 to 0.73 ms from 1K through 64K keys, and tail authentication plus indexing was linear at about 61 microseconds per record. Do not promote the raw reader. Every base point read issued one object range request, and the bounded scan over-read for every affected tail key, reducing 1,024-row throughput from about 196K to 91K rows per second at a 1,024-record tail. Add shared RAM and NVMe caches and a streaming merge before GCS performance work.

hypothesis: A caller-owned decoded RAM cache plus bounded local block cache can remain below authority-root filtering, preserve exact base-plus-certified-tail reads, and remove backend object requests from repeated point and bounded scan paths.
learned: Keep shared cache injection below the authority manifest-binding layer. The repeated point pass made zero backend requests and the 1,024-row scan made one, versus 64 and 80 to 85 on the raw path. Scan throughput improved 1.26x to 1.31x. The combined path adds about 1.6 ms to open and about 200 microseconds to the first miss. Isolate NVMe-only reopen and cache-fault behavior before claiming the full cache hierarchy.

hypothesis: An authority-bound ordered base cursor merged with the resident authenticated txLog tail can make base request amplification depend on emitted rows instead of unrelated tail cardinality while preserving exact ordered reads.
learned: Keep the streaming base-tail merge. The 1,024-record-tail raw scan now makes the same 80 backend range GETs as the zero-tail raw scan and improves from about 91K to 186K rows per second. Shared-cache scans remain at one backend GET. This removes unrelated tail cardinality from base request amplification, but it does not remove the roughly 61 microseconds per record view-open cost or resident memory for the unobjectified tail.

hypothesis: A bounded local block cache can survive authority-view closure and decoded-RAM loss, then serve exact base-plus-certified-tail data after cache-object reconstruction without backend data bytes.
learned: Keep persistent NVMe as the local data tier. After decoded-RAM loss, first-point data and ordered scans transfer zero backend bytes and make zero successful backend range GETs. Do not call this offline reopen: view open still transfers 788 manifest bytes through the backing store, and the first point performs one failed metadata GET.

hypothesis: Corrupted persistent cache parts must never become a non-exact database value; the reader must either fail closed or re-fetch exact range data from the backing store.
learned: Keep the current checksum and repair behavior for the next prototype. Overwriting every persistent data part did not expose corrupt bytes as a value; the focused fixture re-fetched exact range data from the backend. Promote this control into the process suite and add stale-root resurrection before GCS.

hypothesis: Persistent cache contents cannot resurrect a historical root when the exact snapshot lease has drifted, expired, been released, or names another manifest, provided the opener validates against current publication-authority state before storage access.
learned: Keep live-lease validation as a prerequisite for historical cache reopen. Exact release and manifest-mismatch controls refuse before storage access. Do not couple publication-authority generation to immutable-base generation. The next falsifier is a worker given stale authority state or no authority response.

hypothesis: A disposable Range Engine with a warm persistent cache must read current replicated authority after lease release and refuse an old published root before storage access; a stale authority snapshot must be detected by the negative control.
learned: Keep fresh replicated-authority validation in every historical worker bootstrap. The correct path refused every post-release M0 reopen before storage, reclaimed the old compacted closure, and kept M1 exact. Injecting a stale pre-release authority snapshot reopened M0 in every seed and discarded, proving that cached bytes plus an old lease token are not authorization.

hypothesis: A historical Range Engine must fail closed when current replicated authority is unavailable; it must not fall back to cached bytes, an old root, or last-known authority state.
learned: Keep authority unavailability fail-closed. The fifth worker recorded a semantic refusal and opened no historical view when its bounded live-authority read failed. Enabling fallback to a pre-release snapshot reopened M0 in every seed and discarded. The 50 ms deadline is eval configuration, not a production operating claim.

hypothesis: A disposable persistent cache that is overwritten or torn between worker processes must either repair the exact value from authoritative object bytes or refuse; it must never return a non-exact database value.
learned: Keep persistent NVMe as disposable acceleration. Same-length overwrite and half-file truncation both triggered exact backend repair in fresh worker processes. The exercise controls prove the physical faults ran, and the unsafe receipt controls prove the oracle rejects non-exact outcomes. Next prove bounded multi-range eviction before the GCS matrix.

hypothesis: Many logical Range Engines can share one physically bounded persistent cache, lose local blocks under capacity pressure, and still reread every exact value by refilling from the authority-selected immutable object base.
learned: Keep one physically bounded cache per KV Runtime. Eight logical ranges stayed exact after capacity eviction, and reverse rereads required object refills. The unbounded control retained the entire working set and made zero refills, proving the accepted result exercises eviction. Replay the frozen cache-state matrix on objectKV-dev GCS next.

hypothesis: The admitted local eviction contract can select GCS without changing semantic gates, isolate every worker under a unique scratch prefix, and require cleanup before a remote receipt passes.
learned: The GCS execution path is implemented and the local semantic regression remains exact. Do not report a GCS result until an authorized identity verifies the project and bucket, exports OKV_GCP_PROJECT and OKV_GCS_BUCKET, starts required OTLP telemetry, and runs the frozen profile.

hypothesis: A Range Engine can publish fully authenticated immutable tail generations over one unchanged object base while retained readers finish on the old generation, later readers observe the new generation, and stale same-manifest rollback is refused.
learned: Keep immutable Range Engine generations and full-token compare. Coordinated old and new readers remained exact over six same-base publications per seed, and every unsafe control discarded. The pointer swap itself is negligible locally; replacement authentication, sustained read latency, retained-generation memory, failure, and remote economics remain the real performance questions.

hypothesis: An independent KV Runtime can route exact-version point and single-range reads to local Range Engines while refusing stale routing, crossing scans, unavailable snapshots, and requests after worker death.
learned: The independent process hop is not an obvious fatal latency bottleneck in this narrow local profile. Concurrency, cache-state transitions, remote object misses, route refresh, replacement, transport security, telemetry, and PostgreSQL executor integration remain the decision-bearing curves.

hypothesis: A tenant read client can refresh stale range routing, restart a multi-range scan at the original exact version, and merge a complete ordered result across the new split.
learned: Keep bounded client route refresh and complete-scan restart at fixed T. The first process gate proves exact ordered fan-out across a split, but production RangeMap authority, endpoint replacement, concurrent publication, tenant security, remote misses, and PostgreSQL mapping remain open.

hypothesis: The read-only PostgreSQL page adapter can authenticate exact 8 KiB pages through a stale-route refresh and two routed Range Engines while preserving the objectKV version and enforcing an independent PostgreSQL page-LSN frontier.
learned: Keep the two-frontier read contract. The actual adapter path returns authenticated pages across route refresh and range fan-out with sub-millisecond local transport shape, but PostgreSQL callback integration, write ordering, stable barriers, restart recovery, remote objects, and concurrency remain the decision-bearing work.

hypothesis: A pinned PostgreSQL 18.6 process can fill real shared buffers from an authority-bound objectKV relation-page view through smgr_startreadv without falling back to md reads.
learned: The literal PostgreSQL read seam is viable, but PG18 routes sync reads through the AIO callback API. Hot reads remain in PostgreSQL shared buffers; cold read performance now depends on transport reuse, batching, Range Engine cache state, and a real asynchronous objectKV operation. The next semantic gate is page write plus block count under WAL-before-page ordering.

hypothesis: A permanent PostgreSQL page batch can be converted to deterministic objectKV mutations only when PostgreSQL WAL is durable through every page LSN and the expected objectKV view is explicit.
learned: Keep WAL-before-page as an explicit bridge admission boundary. The next decision-bearing slice is authoritative relation extent plus subordinate commit identity, followed by the literal PostgreSQL write and block-count callbacks.

hypothesis: WAL-admitted PostgreSQL pages and authoritative relation-fork extent can commit atomically through a real Cell, resolve duplicate retry to one outcome, and remain exact after leader handoff.
learned: Keep atomic page-plus-extent Cell commits and stable retry identity. The next decision-bearing proof is the literal PostgreSQL write plus nblocks protocol, followed by independent tagged txLog and fresh Range Engine reconstruction before any stable-storage claim.

hypothesis: A pinned PostgreSQL 18.6 process can flush WAL, commit an existing native heap page plus authoritative extent through a subordinate Cell transaction, reconstruct it in a fresh Range Engine, and read the exact result after PostgreSQL restart without writing the local heap file.
learned: Keep the subordinate PostgreSQL WAL to Cell page-commit ordering and fresh Range Engine acknowledgement. The callback seam works, but the current 678 ms debug write shape is dominated by prototype transport and full view reconstruction. Shared version publication plus service restart from objectified base and authenticated txLog is the next decision-bearing slice.

hypothesis: A PostgreSQL backend can distinguish its logical SQL snapshot from the subordinate physical page-store version, learn a checkpointer advance, and continue exact storage operations without weakening explicit stale-version refusal.
learned: Keep PostgreSQL as logical MVCC authority and treat objectKV versions as monotonic physical page-store flush positions. The handshake repairs the immediate live-backend staleness failure. Next remove its discovery-to-operation race and prove sidecar restart from objectified base plus authenticated txLog.

hypothesis: A live PostgreSQL backend can bind each physical page operation atomically to the Cell page store's current immutable view without a discovery round trip, while explicit pinned stale versions still fail closed.
learned: Keep atomic current-generation selection and strict nonzero pins. Removing the discovery operation closes its race and network round trip, but the 688 ms debug checkpoint still reflects serialized Cell commit and full Range Engine reconstruction. The next decision-bearing proof is sidecar restart from an objectified base plus authenticated txLog.

hypothesis: A pinned PostgreSQL 18.6 page service can lose all process memory, recover an exact relation from one immutable object base plus every required signed txLog quorum without reading the source heap, accept another page write, and recover that write after a second service restart.

controls.observed: durable PostgreSQL recovery found no unique txLog quorum
named live SST not found during physical object verification

learned: Keep exact object-base plus signed txLog recovery as the bounded sidecar mechanism. The page service is no longer durable only by process memory or the source heap. The decision-bearing next slice is a replicated authority-selected stable root wired to PostgreSQL stable sync; the local descriptor and deterministic Cell replay are not substitutes for that protocol.

hypothesis: PostgreSQL checkpoint sync can publish the exact recoverable objectKV base-plus-certified-txLog frontier through a replicated authority, reconcile it after page-service restart, and fail closed without advancing the stable root when the authority is unavailable.

controls.observed: PostgreSQL checkpoint request failed after objectKV stable response timed out

learned: Keep PostgreSQL's native sync-request lifecycle and the split between hot txLog durability and replicated stable-root selection. The architecture can fail a checkpoint without losing the newer hot version. Next objectify through the selected version, bind txLog pop to that root, recover the authority itself, and prove remote empty-cache restore before admitting production WAL recycling.

hypothesis: PostgreSQL stable sync can objectify a complete relation, publish the exact closure, pop every required txLog only with replicated authority, recover without a source heap or retained tail, continue writing, and refuse a newer pop when authority is unavailable.

controls.observed: PostgreSQL checkpoint failed after five-second objectKV timeout

learned: Keep the external transaction-authority boundary, versioned complete bases, atomic local root, and publication-authorized txLog pop. The deletion protocol works and fails closed, but the 408 ms debug sync phase for a three-page relation rejects synchronous complete-relation rewrite as the target performance shape. Next move incremental objectification outside the foreground lock, aggregate a database-wide root, recover both authorities, and prove remote empty-cache restore.

hypothesis: Stable target B can publish from base O plus a complete certified txLog suffix while pop stays capped at O.
learned: Keep lagging-base stable roots and object-frontier-capped pop. Reject page-write-triggered full bases and objectifier dependence on the publication state lock.

hypothesis: Checkpoint capture can own one coalesced full-relation objectification job that does not wait for publication authority.

controls.postgres_error: unexpected data beyond EOF in block 3

learned: Checkpoint capture removes object writes from stable publication and bounds full-base creation to one coalesced job per capture. Next implement incremental range or delta objectification, base collection, and publication outside the state lock.

hypothesis: A certified immutable object delta can preserve exact restart semantics while making one-page PostgreSQL updates economical relative to replacement-base rewrites.
learned: The immutable base-plus-delta structure cuts bytes to 8.31 percent of a 1 MiB replacement base and preserves exact restart, but JSON v1 costs 11.11x the changed bytes and is 14 percent slower end to end at this size. Keep the architecture, replace the encoding, and run scale, batch, layer, and GCS curves.

hypothesis: The 65,536-page crossover duration can be measured with the generic bounded counter conversion.

defect.cause: generic bounded_count conversion clamped nanosecond values at 4294967295
defect.impact: durations above 4.294967295 seconds were invalid and the 65536-page ratio could not be used

learned: Convert nanosecond durations through Duration::from_nanos(value).as_secs_f64() and rerun the complete curve.

hypothesis: For one certified 8 KiB page change, immutable delta identity and bytes remain independent of untouched relation size and delta latency crosses full-rewrite latency by 4,096 pages.
learned: Untouched relation size does not change delta identity or bytes. The delta path becomes 2.98x faster at 32 MiB and 4.00x faster at 512 MiB, but activation still scales with the base and JSON v1 remains 11.106x changed bytes.

hypothesis: A fresh PostgreSQL storage worker can authenticate one selected root and complete delta lineage, open an exact immutable view, and serve the first point without work proportional to untouched relation bytes.
learned: The previous 4.549-second restart result measured whole-relation work, not the first OLTP read. Manifest-bound view readiness remained below 5 ms at 512 MiB and first reads stayed flat, while full audit and oracle scan scaled with bytes. Next prove remote integrity and economics on GCS before changing production serving policy.

hypothesis: An authority-selected exact-revision closure can preserve exact lazy reads while RAM and persistent NVMe remove provider data requests from a bounded hot working set.
hard_gates: local dimensions, reads, identity, receipts, cache states, replay, bounds, and six controls passed

decisions.next_gate: gcs cache states, OTel, cleanup, reuse distance

learned: Exact provider revision checks preserve sub-millisecond local cached reads. Persistent NVMe removes data GETs after reopen but retains two metadata GETs. Cloud viability still depends on GCS p99 and realistic cache reuse.

hypothesis: Passive demand caching with no more than 25 percent persistent NVMe can hold provider misses at or below 2.5 percent under named skewed and moving-hotset traces.
hard_gates: all semantic, identity, bounded-cache, trace, replay, RSS, and cleanup gates passed; the economic lane constraint failed; all four unsafe controls discarded
learned: The authenticated RAM and NVMe hit path remains fast, but passive bounded demand caching misses far too often to meet either request-cost or p99 targets at a 25-percent local-data fraction. Explicit locality is now required.

hypothesis: A provider miss ratio at or below 2.5 percent is feasible with ideal capacity-respecting placement for the RFC 0067 uniform, Zipfian 0.99, and moving-hotset distributions at a 25-percent local-data fraction.
hard_gates: all correct probability, independent enumeration, capacity, complement, request-cost, deterministic-replay, budget, and schema gates passed; the unchanged economic lane constraint discarded all three pairs; all three unsafe controls discarded
learned: The passive policy has avoidable regret, but no cache policy can meet the frozen 2.5-percent target for these workload-capacity pairs. Hot service must be conditioned on explicit placed range coverage or the product must change local fraction, traffic concentration, tiering, or scope.
